On this page

Managing Runs from Chat ​

Everything the Runs UI does is also a tool PRIME can call, so you can drive a run entirely from chat.

Find it ​

ToolUse
list_runsRecent runs with status, project, and preview
search_runsFull-text across briefs and threads
get_runOne run's detail — thread, checklist, participants, usage
search_activityAcross runs: what happened, when, by whom

Steer it ​

Reply into a run with reply_to_run. This is how you answer an agent's question — PRIME relays it back to whoever asked, in the same session, so no context is lost.

Control it with control_run:

ActionEffect
pauseStops after the current step; fully resumable
resumePicks up from where it paused
haltStops the run (cancelled)
reopenBrings a done/error/cancelled run back to active
deleteRemoves it

Pausing is not the same as halting. A paused run keeps every participant session and branch, so resuming costs nothing but the next turn.

Resolve an approval ​

When a project's policy is approval: confirm, a write parks the run at awaiting_input holding a PendingApproval that names the target project, the exact task, and the question.

resolve_run_approval(runId, approvalId, decision: "approve" | "deny", note?)

Approving re-runs that exact delegation with approved: true. Denying records the decision and hands control back to PRIME, which will re-plan around it rather than retrying blindly.

Approve the change, not the sentence

The gate is structured on purpose. A free-text "yes" in chat is ambiguous about which pending change it refers to when more than one is queued.

Read the evidence ​

For any completed task, three things are worth checking, in this order:

  1. verification — the verdict, and by. A by: 'command' pass is a real exit code. A by: 'model' pass is a second opinion on the report. by: 'none' means nothing checkable was available — treat that task as unverified.
  2. evidenceManifest.changes — the branch, the base it was cut from, the commits, and per-file additions/deletions, read off git by the engine rather than reported by the agent.
  3. evidenceManifest.commands — each command, its exit code, and its output tail.

The run-level verificationLog is the append-only record. If a task disappeared from the checklist between amendments, its verdicts are still there.

Watch the cost ​

get_run returns the usageLog: one entry per settled LLM call with actor, models, token counts, cost, and duration. Two flags matter when the numbers look wrong:

  • unpriced on an entry — tokens were spent but the provider never reported a price.
  • unreported on a usage record — the call ran and no request reported a token. Those zeros are the absence of a measurement, not a measurement of zero.

Per-message stats also carry costShared: true when a cost is this message's share of a turn total rather than a quoted per-call price. The UI says so rather than presenting an estimate as an invoice.

Hand files back and forth ​

  • attach_run_assets — attach files an agent produced to the run.
  • send_file — deliver a file to you in chat; it renders as an image or a download.

Run assets live under memory/runs/<id>/assets/ and are served through the run-asset endpoint.

Share it ​

A run has an owner (createdBy) and a sharedWith list. Viewers can watch the thread; steering stays with the owner and admins holding runs.steerAll. Admins with runs.viewAll see every run regardless.
